title: Gas Price Predictor
shortDescription: An end-to-end forecasting app: an automated data pipeline, a PostgreSQL store and an XGBoost model that predicts gas prices days ahead.
description: An end-to-end machine learning application for forecasting retail gas prices. An automated pipeline collects weekly public government data and loads it into a PostgreSQL database, building a clean historical record. An XGBoost model trained on that history produces a multi-day forecast with a median estimate and 25–75% and 10–90% uncertainty ranges. The interactive Streamlit dashboard charts actual prices against the forecast, reports model accuracy against a naive baseline, flags periods of likely volatility and turns a visitor's local pump price into a local prediction. The app is hosted on Render, so the first visit can take a moment while it starts.

technicalDetails.problem: Forecast near-term retail gas prices, with an honest picture of how uncertain each forecast is.
technicalDetails.dataset: Weekly public government gas price data, collected by an automated pipeline and stored in PostgreSQL.
technicalDetails.approach: Train an XGBoost model on the historical series, forecast several days ahead with median and interval estimates, and measure accuracy against a naive baseline.
technicalDetails.architecture: Data pipeline → PostgreSQL → XGBoost model → Streamlit dashboard on Render.
results: Mean absolute error of $0.073, versus $0.155 for the naive baseline.
Forecasts shown with 25–75% and 10–90% ranges, plus a local price prediction from the visitor's own pump price.
